files.why: Framework-free Role union (incl. "finance") and CurrentUser type — the identity taxonomy no slice currently owns.
Zod DTO for the current-user/session endpoint, kept private to data/ per the DTO-stays-home rule.
Map the current-user DTO to the core CurrentUser so DTO shapes never leak upward.
fetchCurrentUser via shared httpTransport — the IO that supplies the caller's role.
MSW handler returning a mock current user with a role, since the app is MSW-mocked and no auth backend exists.
Cached reactive session state (current user/role) — shared across views, so a data/ store like billing's.
Expose the current user's role reactively to feature UI without leaking data/ internals.
Required 5th slice entry; exports an (empty) route list re-exported by index.ts per the structure test.
The slice's only public surface: Role type, useCurrentUser, identityMockHandlers, identityRoutes.
Gate canVoidInvoice on finance role via the @slices/identity public alias, combined with existing canVoid(invoice) — the documented cross-slice pattern.
Register identityMockHandlers so the current-user endpoint is served in dev/test.
Concatenate identityRoutes for consistency with how every slice's routes are composed (even if empty).

uncertain: Home for current-user/role: I placed it in a new `identity` slice (matches "everything lives in a slice" and the worked-example-2 cross-slice consumption pattern), but it could defensibly live in `shared/` as cross-cutting infrastructure like httpTransport, or in an `app/` provider. No precedent exists, so this is a real architecture-review call and drives most of the file list.

Where the finance gate lives: I kept it in billing/ui/composables/useInvoiceDetail.ts (composing existing canVoid + role), which keeps billing/core free of a cross-slice dependency. The alternative — extend billing/core/policy.ts to canVoid(invoice, role) for purity — would pull the identity Role type sideways into core, which feels like a layering smell.

Shape of the current-user source: a data/ store (session cache) vs a load-once composable/query. I chose a store since role is app-wide shared state, but the README notes stores are deliberately rare.
Whether app/router/index.ts truly needs identityRoutes: the identity slice has no pages, but index.ts must still re-export routes.ts to satisfy the structure test, so the export exists regardless.
questions: Where does the current user's role actually come from? There is no auth/session/login anywhere today — is there a real backend endpoint, JWT, or SSO to read, or should this stay MSW-mocked for now?
Is hiding the button sufficient, or must voiding also be enforced server-side? Client-only hiding is not security — should the void mutation / MSW handler reject non-finance callers too?
Can a user hold multiple roles or is there a hierarchy (e.g. admin implies finance), or is it a single exact-match role?
For non-finance users, hide the button entirely (as requested) or render it disabled with a tooltip?
Is introducing a first identity/auth concept (a whole new slice) acceptable scope for this request, given CODEOWNERS-protected structure/consistency tests will gate a new slice?
